pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: Browser configuration now supports selecting the Chrome remote-debugging port and consistently uses it when probing, launching, and connecting to Chrome. User-supplied Chrome binaries are now launched with an argument-vector subprocess API rather than a shell-oriented API. The agent and file-upload edits appear non-semantic. Actual deployment impact depends on callers selecting the affected browser setup paths and, for the new capability, configuring a non-default port.

behavior_changes.description: Callers using a supplied Chrome binary can choose a remote-debugging port; browser reuse checks, the newly launched Chrome argument, and the CDP connection target use that configured port rather than a fixed endpoint.
evidence: The configured port is interpolated into the local version endpoint, Chrome launch argument, and Playwright CDP endpoint.

behavior_changes.description: A supplied Chrome executable is now started directly with separate executable and argument values. This avoids shell command interpretation and allows the generated remote-debugging option to be passed as an individual argument.
evidence: The executable path is passed separately from chrome_launch_args to create_subprocess_exec.
The resulting process PID continues to be wrapped by psutil for lifecycle management.

behavior_changes.description: The built-in browser launch path now derives its remote-debugging argument and port-conflict check from BrowserConfig. If the configured local port is already occupied, that debugging argument is omitted as before, but for the selected port rather than specifically port 9222.
evidence: The debugging option was separated from the static Chrome argument list.
The built-in launch path constructs and conditionally removes the option using the configured port.

important_symbols.reason: Defines the new caller-visible port setting, its default, and its nullable type; all launch and connection behavior depends on this value.
Contains the main observable change: configured-port discovery and CDP connection plus direct subprocess launching of a supplied Chrome binary.
Propagates the configured port into the built-in launch path and its occupied-port handling.
Centralizes formatting of the Chrome debugging argument after it was removed from the static CHROME_ARGS collection.
Documents the intended custom-port contract, although its HTTP mocking appears inconsistent with the production dependency.

investigation_hints.description: Trace every construction and validation path for BrowserConfig to determine who can select browser_binary_path, chrome_remote_debugging_port, or conflicting extra Chrome arguments.
Inspect the lifecycle around local CDP probing, Chrome process creation, retries, reuse, and shutdown, including concurrent Browser instances using distinct or identical ports.
Check the contract with Chrome and Playwright for remote-debugging argument precedence, default bind address, occupied ports, and connecting to an existing process.

local_risks.description: BrowserConfig explicitly permits chrome_remote_debugging_port=None, but setup code interpolates that value into URLs and passes it to socket operations. A caller using the allowed null value can therefore produce an invalid endpoint or a socket argument error instead of obtaining a browser.

A caller can supply another --remote-debugging-port value through extra_browser_args. Because only exact duplicates are removed and the launch arguments are assembled in a set whose order is acknowledged as not guaranteed, Chrome may select a port different from the one subsequently probed and used for CDP connection.
